newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Belgium to present debt management programme Jan.8.
newsitem.headline: Belgium to present debt management programme Jan.8.

text.p: Belgian Finance Minister Philippe Maystadt will present details of the country's long awaited debt management programme to a parliamentary committee meeting on January 8, a Treasury official said on Tuesday.

The programme will be based on recommendations from Morgan Stanley and UBS, who were appointed by the government last July to look at, respectively, the risk profile and potential for savings in the country's 10,000 billion Belgian franc mountain of debt.
The programme is aimed at establishing portfolio benchmarks to guide servicing the debt.

1997 will be an important year for the Belgian Treasury. The government has committed itself to bringing the country's debt down to around 127 percent of gross domestic product (GDP) from a forecast 130.4 percent at the end of 1996 and 137 percent at the end of 1993.
The bulk of the reduction is planned to be achieved by repaying foreign currency borrowings with 222 billion Belgian francs of proceeds of past central bank gold sales.
It hopes this will be enough for the European single currency's criterion on debt reduction, which says debt should be below or approaching 60 percent of GDP at a "satisfactory pace."
Belgium's towns and regions have also been urged to use 32 billion francs generated by the bourse listing of bank Dexia CC to reduce their debt, thereby helping the country's overall debt position.
Other public bodies have been urged to put cash balances into government bonds.
